transcript:
Header: 2026-11-18 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 1:15:00 | Location: All Hands - Virtual
Attendees: Avery Park (CEO), Maya Chen (Head of Engineering), Diego Ruiz (Head of Product), Elena Kaur (Head of Ops), Samir Patel (VP Sales), R&D and company-wide attendees (100+)

Summary: Avery opens with Q4 performance and velocity highlights; Maya covers runtime improvements and Dedicated capacity news; Diego walks through Private 2.0 timeline and Redwood Optimize updates; Elena covers hiring and org changes; Q&A covers SOC2, private deployment timelines, and cost/latency tradeoffs.

00:00 Avery: Hey everyone, welcome to the November all-hands, appreciate you carving out time. Quick housekeeping  slides are in the chat, recording will be posted. We'll go through updates, then Q&A.
00:22 Avery: High level, Q4 is looking strong, ARR motion is ahead of plan, churn continues to be low. We signed three mid-market Dedicated deals last month and a larger private pilot with a financial customer, so big kudos to sales and solutions.
01:15 Samir: yes thanks, team  the dedicated deals are a mix of reserved and hybrid, a lot of the asks were around throughput SLAs and KV cache persistence, we leaned on the new autoscale policies.
01:50 Maya: quick eng update  we've shipped the kernel selector improvements; customers are seeing steady 12-18% token-per-second gains in our benchmarks, though some workloads had regressions with extreme seq lengths, so we're rolling a tuned path.
02:40 Diego: regarding Private 2.0  roadmap is focused on private control plane, better KMS integrations, and a simpler on-prem bundle; plan is canary with two customers in December, general availability in Q1 2027 pending SOC 2 closure.
03:30 Elena: hiring  we have approvals to add 10 ICs across infra and product and two senior SEs; People Ops will circulate job postings and interview panels.
04:05 Audience (multiple): applause, chatter
05:00 Avery: product/ops priorities for next quarter: 1) finish SOC 2; 2) tighten Dedicated latency SLOs; 3) ship Private 2.0 canary; 4) expand Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization profiles.
06:10 Maya: on optics of performance  we put together a public benchmark doc, but note that some model names got munged in export, so we'll correct the names; current near-term work is kernel vectorization and better KV prefetch which reduces cold-starts.
07:00 Diego: on roadmap cadence  we're shifting to monthly ship lanes instead of big quarterly drops; this should help customers test and adopt incrementally and reduce regression blast radius.
08:30 Audience Q: any details on pricing for Dedicated? Samir: short answer  pricing tiers largely unchanged; we'll send detailed pricing grid post call, there will be volume discounts and burst credits in the new packages.
09:10 Question on Private timelines: Diego: canary in December with two customers, GA Q1 2027, documentation and deployment playbooks will land in the repo a week before the canary.
10:00 Question on SOC 2 bits: Elena: remediations for a couple control gaps are in flight, KMS/HSM integration is on the list, we expect audit completion by end of December if no major findings.
11:00 Technical interjection (Maya): rolling fallback policies  we now support model variant fallback to keep apps online during capacity spikes; it's been tested in staging but we want 1-2 customer pilots before broad enablement.
12:10 Avery: on go-to-market  PLG continues to be our engine, but we are increasing enablement for dedicated and private sales plays; channel partnerships in APAC are progressing.
13:40 Samir: customer wins  highlight customer 'NovaHealth' who moved to Dedicated for throughput, and 'BlueFin' who started a private pilot for compliance.
14:20 Audience: cheers
15:00 Deep-dive: Maya shows a short clip of kernel perf charts  some transcripts show 'kernel' as 'canal' in slides, haha, we'll fix that.
20:00 Question: is Redwood Optimize going to recommend quantization by default? Diego: Optimize will suggest profiles with expected latency/cost delta; defaults will be conservative, opt-in for risky quant settings.
24:00 Question: data residency and encryption  Elena: Private supports customer KMS, audit logs are on by default for Private, for Hosted API we'll add more granular retention controls next quarter.
28:00 Question from engineering: any freeze on infra changes for canary? Maya: we'll have a 2-week freeze window around canary rollouts and a rollback plan.
32:00 People Ops note (Elena): compensation cycle is next month, managers will receive calibration packets. Also update on parental leave policy  extended to 16 weeks.
38:00 Q&A rapid fire: some questions about model catalog naming, model calibration, evals  Diego and Maya answer briefly and note follow-ups.
50:00 Avery: closing remarks  focus on reliability and measurable unit economics. we compete on serving not just model quality.
51:10 Avery: thank you, short recap of actions then we'll take more detailed questions in breakout channels.
55:00 Post-meeting: leadership stayed for an extra 20 minutes for targeted region update (APAC channels) and for a sales enablement sync.

Action items (verbatim from chat):
- Maya Chen: post Dedicated perf summary in #eng by 2026-11-25
- Diego Ruiz: publish Private 2.0 timeline doc by 2026-12-02
- Elena Kaur: coordinate SOC 2 remediation runbook by 2026-11-30
- Samir Patel: send pricing grid and Dedicated packages by 2026-11-22
